title: Exploration Tree
description: DISCOVER-stage artifact from the research-trajectory-extractor seat: the research TRAJECTORY that produced a method, not the method itself. Three node types — dead_end (an approach the paper tried and abandoned), decision (a design choice with real alternatives), pivot (a change of direction and the observation that forced it). dead_end is the most valuable type, because it is the part that saves a future reader from rediscovering a known failure; ablation rows showing that a component HURTS are dead ends. Every node carries support_level: `explicit` when the paper directly reports it (then source_refs must name the section / table / figure), or `inferred` when the node is reconstructed from the narrative. HONESTY RULE, encoded here and in the prompt: PREFER OMISSION OVER FABRICATING A HIGHLY SPECIFIC INFERRED NODE — an invented dead end is worse than a missing one, because a future reader will trust it. Companion to method_teardown, never a replacement: method_teardown records what the method IS, this records how it came to be.

source_ref.description: The paper this trajectory was extracted from ([[slug]], DOI, arXiv id, URL, or run-local path). Non-blank.

nodes.description: The trajectory nodes. MAY be empty: a paper that genuinely reports no abandoned approach, no alternative and no pivot yields an empty tree, and that is an honest finding. An empty tree on a paper that DOES report ablations is an incomplete teardown, which the quality auditor reads as a gap.

support_level.description: explicit = the paper directly reports it (cite the section/table/figure in source_refs); inferred = reconstructed from the narrative.

summary.description: One line: what this node is.

failure_mode.description: dead_end: why it failed, concretely — 'did not work' is not a failure mode.

lesson.description: dead_end: what transfers to somebody else's problem.

choice.description: decision: the design choice that was made.

alternatives.description: decision: the alternatives genuinely considered (at least one).

informed_by.description: decision: what evidence informed the choice.

from_state.description: pivot: what the work was doing before.

trigger.description: pivot: the observation that forced the change ('we initially pursued X but found ...' is the tell).

source_refs.description: Section / table / figure locators. REQUIRED to be non-empty when support_level is explicit.

relates_to.description: Optional cross-reference into the method_teardown or claim ids this node bears on.

extraction_note.description: Optional: what the paper's narrative did or did not make recoverable (e.g. 'no ablation table; every node is inferred').
